events.title: TrueGrass with Flutes & Low
events.description: TrueGrass!® with opening actFlutes & LowTrueGrass! brings tight harmonies, lively picking, and a love of classic bluegrass to the stage, blending traditional favorites with modern material and originals. The band features Tom Draughon on guitar, clawhammer banjo, and lead vocals; Jed Malischke on banjo and dobro; Bruce Qualey on bass; and Carol McDowall on fiddle—and they all sing!Opening the evening is Flutes & Low, the folk duo of Ben Pichler and Cambria Haen. Since meeting in Duluth, they’ve crafted a sound inspired by the Midwest’s landscapes, pairing two voices with simple arrangements and memorable melodies.

events.description: Fall is here, winter is around the corner, and we’re getting ready for ski season at Spirit Mountain. Parking:Attendees can park at the base of the mountain at the Grand Avenue Chalet parking lot: 8551 Grand Avenue, Duluth, MN 55808 Come enjoy the fall colors, grab your pass, and spend a fall afternoon on the mountain. More event details to come as it is confirmed.

events.title: Teacher Training Workshop – Spring Weekend
events.description: Spring Weekend Workshop Join us for our Teacher Training Institute’s (almost) Spring workshop! Learn from Wolf Ridge Naturalists to co-teach in this transitional season of weather (snow, rain), develop your naturalist skills and learn tips and tricks for teaching in the cold. No prior outdoor learning experience needed! Great for those just starting out or those that have already been integrating outdoor learning into their teaching practices. Bring the family! Wolf Ridge provides daytime outdoor activities for youth (must be accompanied by an adult) or can recommend local spots for spring adventures. On Saturday evening, participants can experience Wolf Ridge’s outdoor adventure ropes course.

events.title: Teacher Training Workshop – Winter Weekend
events.description: Winter Weekend Workshop Join us for our Teacher Training Institute’s winter workshop! Learn from Wolf Ridge Naturalists to co-teach with the snow, develop your naturalist skills and learn tips and tricks for teaching in the cold. No prior outdoor learning experience needed! Great for those just starting out or those that have already been integrating outdoor learning into their teaching practices. Bring the family! Wolf Ridge provides daytime outdoor activities for youth (must be accompanied by an adult) or can recommend local spots for winter adventures. On Saturday evening, participants can experience Wolf Ridge’s outdoor adventure ropes course- the more snow, the better!

events.title: Language Advisory Board Event: Izhi-ganawendamang Gidinwewininaan Bapashkominitigong
events.description: Please join Nagaajiwanaang Genawendangig Anishinaabemowin for Izhi-ganawendamang Gidinwewininaan Bapashkominitigong with Giizhibimi-ayaakwe miinawaa Niizhoodewin. We’ll talk about our experiences and different paths of learning as children and young adults, and the ways we integrate our passions for language learning and teaching into the Fond du Lac community through various work. We’ll also talk about the importance of this work and impacts it has had on our lives as young language speakers.

events.description: Join the Nation’s Top Cross-Country Skiers in Cable, WI for a week of world-class competition.

events.title: Seeley Hills Classic
events.description: Ski the historic Seeley Hills Classic and take part in a rich Northwoods ski tradition. The winding, wooded classic ski race is the second-largest annual classic cross-country ski event held on the Birkebeiner Trail.

events.title: Ski de She Camp & Race
events.description: Ski de She is a time for women to come together to expand their skills, build race confidence, and connect with fellow female skiers. Choose to attend our 3-day camp or compete in the adjoining race, or both! Ski with friends. Ski for health. Ski with confidence.

events.title: 2027 American Birkebeiner Ski Week Events
events.description: Be a part of a legend! The Slumberland American Birkebeiner is North America’s largest and most prestigious cross-country ski race. Skiers make their way from Cable to Hayward, WI, on the legendary Birkie Trail, finishing on the snow-covered Main Street of Hayward, WI. Enjoy a week full of racing, live music, food, and ski events in the Northwoods. An estimated 40,000 skiers & spectators will attend Birkie week festivities. Don’t miss it!

events.title: Cook County Historical Society Annual Meeting with Guest Speaker Keith Morris
events.address: Johnson Heritage Post, 115 Wisconsin Street, Grand Marais, MN, 55604, United States
events.description: Join the Cook County Historical Society (CCHS) on October 27 for its Annual Meeting, with keynote speaker Keith Morris. This event is free and open to the public, with donations graciously accepted. Morris will talk about his new book, “Growing Up on the Gunflint Trail,” which chronicles over a century of his family's life along the iconic Minnesota road, detailing his upbringing at Poplar Lake and the neighboring Nor'wester Lodge. During the business portion of the event, CCHS staff and board members will share updates from the past year and ask members to vote on potential new board of directors. (While the event is free and open to the public, only CCHS members are eligible to vote.) Not yet a member? Become one here: cookcountyhistory.org/support.

events.title: Spirit of the Wilderness Community Art Show, "The Art of Sabbath," Opening Reception
events.address: Johnson Heritage Post Art Gallery, 115 W. Wisconsin Street, Grand Marais, MN, 55604, United States
events.description: The Johnson Heritage Post Art Gallery is pleased to host the 15th annual Spirit of the Wilderness Community Art Show, themed "The Art of Sabbath." This gallery exhibition centers around winter in the north, which is a time of survival: physically, mentally, and spiritually. This exhibit explores how artists navigate the season, whether hibernating, ice fishing, or moving south, and looks at how we not only survive, but thrive, during the northern winter. Drawing on the ancient practice of Sabbath, participating artists showcase how they rest, recover, and restore through physical stillness and spiritual reconnection. The resulting works highlight these personal reflections across all mediums. The exhibit opens with a public reception on Friday, November 6, 2026, from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m., and runs through November 29, 2026.

events.title: Best Stargazing November

events.description: New moon nights – night when the moon is absent from the sky – make for great stargazing. events.title: Taurids Meteor Shower
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: The Taurids meteor shower is an annual meteor shower that occurs every November and is composed of two streams, the Southern Taurids and the Northern Taurids. The Taurids are known for producing bright fireballs, and 2025 is predicted to be a year with an increased number of them At peak viewing times during the Taurid meteor shower, you may be able to see about a half-dozen shooting stars per hour. The Northern Taurids are active between Oct 20 - Dec 10 and peak on Nov. 9-12.

events.title: Leonids Meteor Shower
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: The Leonids meteor shower offers clear-sky meteor rates of about 10 to 15 shooting stars per hour. They are active between Nov. 6 - 30 and will peak on Nov. 17-18. The Leonids are bright meteors and have a high percentage of persistent trains according to AMS. The Leonids' radiant is located in the sickle-shaped head of the constellation Leo, the lion. Leonid meteor hunting can be incredible, or a total bust. It all depends on where its parent body, Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, will be in its orbit and the kind of debris clumps that will be around when our planet passes through this comet's orbit.

events.title: November Full Moon
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: 1st of 3 supermoons in a row A perigee is when the moon 's orbit is closest to the earth and a supermoon is when the full or new moon coincide (or almost coincide) with the perigee. What does that mean? The moon looks exceptionally big because it is close! Full moons have many names derived from various cultures reflecting what was happening in the natural world. While the Frost Moon and Freezing Moon are self-explanatory, November's full moon is most known as the Beaver Moon. Beavers are quite active preparing for winter. Also known as the Mourning Moon, due to the increase in darkness.

events.title: Geminids Meteor Shower
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: The Geminids meteor shower occurs between November 19 to December 24 and this year will peak on the nights of December 13 and 14. The shower can produce 130 to 140 bright, white, fast meteors per hour on a clear sky. The debris that falls onto Earth's atmosphere during this meteor shower comes from the asteroid Phaethon. The meteor shower's radiant is located in the constellation Gemini, which rises around sunset.

events.title: December Full Moon
events.address: North Shore, MN 61, Silver Bay, MN, 55614, United States
events.description: 2nd of 3 supermoons in a row A perigee is when the moon 's orbit is closest to the earth and a supermoon is when the full or new moon coincide (or almost coincide) with the perigee. What does that mean? The moon looks exceptionally big because it is close! Full moons have many names derived from various cultures reflecting what was happening in the natural world. December's full moon is known as the Cold Moon or Long Nights Moon. In addition to the shortest daylight day of the year, the Long Nights Moon pertains to the amount of time the moon is above the horizon. It takes a high trajectory across the sky because it is opposite to the low sun.

events.title: January Full Moon

events.description: 3rd of 3 supermoons A perigee is when the moon 's orbit is closest to the earth and a supermoon is when the full or new moon coincide (or almost coincide) with the perigee. What does that mean? The moon looks exceptionally big because it is close! Full moons have many names derived from various cultures reflecting what was happening in the natural world. The January full moon is most often known as the Wolf Moon because it is the month hungry wolves howl in the night. It is also known as the Stay Home, or Quiet, Moon as cold temps set in and we want to snuggle in and stay home.

events.title: Theatre North Presents: The Dining Room
events.description: The opening production for the 2026 – 2027 Theatre North Season is The Dining Room. Synopsis: Set in the dining room of a typical well-to-do household, The Dining Room is a mosaic of interrelated scenes – some funny, some touching, some rueful – which, taken together, create an in-depth portrait of vanishing traditions of the American upper middle class. The actors change roles, as they portray a wide variety of characters, from little boys to stern grandfathers, and from giggling teenage girls to Irish housemaids. Each vignette introduces a new set of people and events (spanning decades): a father lectures his son on grammar and politics; a boy returns from boarding school to discover his mother’s infidelity; a senile grandmother doesn’t recognize her own sons at Christmas dinner; a daughter, her marriage a shambles, pleads futilely to return home. Dovetailing swiftly and smoothly, the varied scenes coalesce, ultimately, into a theatrical experience of exceptional range, compassionate humor and abundant humanity. Show Times are: November 5, 6, 7, 13 and 14 at 7:00pm Matinees November 8 and 15 at 2:00pm TICKET INFORMATION IS FOUND HERE.

events.title: Introduction to Designing and Building Cutting and Charcuterie Boards
events.address: 5503 W. Range View Drive, Hurley, WI
events.description: Here’s an introductory course for anyone who wants to learn how to work with hardwoods and has little or no knowledge of the process. In the Fe University course “Introduction to Designing and Building Cutting and Charcuterie Boards,” spend a concentrated weekend Nov. 7-8 in the Hurley High School Woodshop learning from Tim Lutgen how to work with mixed hardwoods, lay out your project, select the best wood, perform all machining under the experienced guidance, glue up, add edging and/or handles, and finish your custom creation. Best of all, you’ll be able to show off your own beautiful hardwood creation to family and friends for years to come, or gift it to loved ones for the holiday season! Class is limited to 12 students. Register by Oct. 23 to get a $5 Early Bird discount off the regular registration price of $45! (The registration price does not include materials and required personal safety equipment.) Learn more and register at https://www.feuniversity.com/class/ Fe University – Introduction to Designing and Building Cutting and Charcuterie Boards with Tim Lutgen Nov. 7-8, 2026, 9 a.m.-4 p.m. Hurley High School, 5503 W. events.title: Underground Critters: Herptiles and Mammals
events.description: This informative, entertaining Fe University course on the consecutive Tuesday afternoons of Nov. 10 and 17 in Mercer will teach you about the mammals, reptiles and amphibians that inhabit the Northwoods. Come away with a better understanding of how to identify these critters, where to find them, and how they survive conditions from harsh, cold winters to hot, dry summers. Hannah Thorpe will help you learn how to identify the reptiles and amphibians that share the Northwoods with us, their behavioral and physical adaptations, habitats, and ecology. With Jenna Malinowski, you’ll find out the important ecological roles small mammals such as rodents, bats, and lagomorphs play in conservation, and much more! Only $20 per person. Learn more and register at https://www.feuniversity.org/class/ ! Fe University: Jenna Malinowski and Hannah Thorpe – Underground Critters: Herptiles and Mammals Nov. 10 and 17, 2026, 1-2:30 p.m. Mercer Community Center, 2648W Margaret St., Mercer, Wis.

events.title: Theatre North Presents: Our Town
events.description: Theatre North Presents: Our Town, by Thornton Wilder, Directed by: Helen Fashbaugh Show Dates and Times: February 18, 19, 20, 26 and 27 at 7:00pm Matinees February 21 and 28 at 2:00pm Thornton Wilder’s American classic, Pultizer-prize winning Our Town, explores the universal human experience of life, love, and death. Set in the fictional small town of Grover’s Corners, New Hampshire, the story follows the everyday lives of the Gibbs and Webb families across three acts. The play is famous for its minimalist approach, often performed on a bare stage with no curtains or scenery, relying on pantomime and a narrator called the Stage Manager to guide the audience into its intimacy and truth. The narrative is divided into three distinct acts: Act I: Daily Life: Introduces the town’s routine, highlighting the simple chores, gossip, and rhythms of small-town life. Act II: Love and Marriage: Follows the childhood friends, George Gibbs and Emily Webb, as they fall in love, grow up, and get married. Act III: Death and Eternity: Concludes years later with Emily’s tragic death in childbirth.

events.title: ACLARA Meeting
events.description: Aitkin County Lakes and Rivers Association (aka ACLARA) represents 20 lake associations in Aitkin County. Founded in 2005, ACLARA brings together lake/river associations throughout Aitkin County for the purpose of educating members on keeping its lakes/rivers and shore land healthy for future generations. Meetings are held on the second Saturday, April through October, usually at the Aitkin County Library stating at 9:30 a.m. Members are encouraged to discuss their association’s issues, if any, and share ideas on lake/river management, water quality and conservation matters that impact the waters we all appreciate and enjoy. Communication to the membership is via email. Annual, nonrefundable dues are $25 for one representative and one or two alternates. Dues cover the costs of any pertinent information to keep members informed on important issues, local expert speakers on a variety of topics at the monthly meetings and minimal administrative costs. Individuals who share a common interest in the well-being of our lakes/rivers and are not part of an active lake/river association may also join annually for $25.

events.title: Ecstatic Dance Grand Marais | Harvest Dance
events.venue: Cook County Community Center | Log Cabin
events.address: Cook County Community Center | Log Cabin
events.description: Ecstatic Dance Grand Marais | Harvest Dance Monday, October 26, 7:00 - 8:30 p.m. Cook County Community Center | Log Cabin What is Ecstatic Dance? An intentional, judgement-free space for free-form movement without words. An invitation to embodiment, fun, healing, flow, and play. What's the general flow of the event? 7:00 pm: Warm-up set with slower tunes. Stretching and moving into a deeper embodied awareness. 7:15 pm: Brief opening circle. Grand Marais Ecstatic Dance will speaks to the intention and framework of the event. Everyone is asked to share their name and optionally share an intention for the dance. 7:25 pm or so: Full set begins. The music generally starts and ends with a slower pace and intensity, with a peak in the middle. 8:30 pm or so: Closing circle. We breathe together and have the option to share what arose for us during the dance and share community announcements. We encourage arriving for the warm-up set and opening circle. We think of it as an important transition into our co-created space where we can leave our days' activities behind and greet the moment more presently. And, you will never be turned away for arriving later!

events.title: Full Moon Poetry
events.description: Full Moon Poetry Drury Lane Books, Grand Marais Monthly (see dates below), 6 - 8 p.m. Everyone is invited to participate in this open mic style reading. While we focus on poetry, the broader goal is human connection - don’t feel pressured to participate or strictly read poetry! Sometimes we get to watch the moon rise over the lake, sometimes we have guest poets, but we always have a great time. Our usual facilitator is Bookseller Kestrel. Please contact them if you are interested in leading a full moon session! We meet at the fire circle on the beach, behind Drury Lane Books in downtown Grand Marais. Upcoming dates: 10/26/2026 Monday 11/24/2026 Tuesday Expect to be indoors if the weather is rainy, winds are high, or temps are below 15 degrees F. The only time we will cancel this event is if there are severe travel advisories, or an unexpected emergency occurs. Accessibility: Due to the beach rock, walking aids and wheelchairs may have difficulty.

events.title: Cook County Historical Society Annual Meeting with Guest Speaker Keith Morris
events.description: Join the Cook County Historical Society (CCHS) on October 27 for its Annual Meeting, with keynote speaker Keith Morris. This event is free and open to the public, with donations graciously accepted. Morris will talk about his new book, “Growing Up on the Gunflint Trail,” which chronicles over a century of his family's life along the iconic Minnesota road, detailing his upbringing at Poplar Lake and the neighboring Nor'wester Lodge. During the business portion of the event, CCHS staff and board members will share updates from the past year and ask members to vote on potential new board of directors. (While the event is free and open to the public, only CCHS members are eligible to vote.) Not yet a member?

events.title: While there was unfortunately no snow
events.description: While there was unfortunately no snow on November 21, the lighting of the Jack Frost Tree that evening evidently helped, because today, November 25, it is snowing in Ironwood! Forecast shows a gradual temperature drop going forward as well, so we just hope that this becomes reality and a true Jack Frost Wintertime can arrive at last! Jack Frost Festival Parade of Lights is on Saturday, December 7th, at 6:00 p.m., and the full list of Jack Frost events and activities can be found on this website by clicking on “events” and going to “Jack Frost Festival.”

events.title: Little Explorers: Cozy Dens & Winter Homes
events.description: Little Explorers is an exciting morning of stories, crafts, songs, and nature activities geared towards 3–6 year olds at Hunt Hill; though all ages are welcome! Every program starts in the Lower Level of the Richard Grand Recreation Hall at Hunt Hill Nature Center, unless otherwise noted. Guardians must stay for the duration of the program, and each program will feature a different nature theme. Depending on weather, we will be outside for a portion of this program. Please dress appropriately to be inside and outside in the weather. In November, Explorers will learn about hibernation and the many ways animals prepare for winter as we explore dens, winter homes, and survival strategies through stories, hands-on building, and imaginative play. Read The Bear Snores On by Karma Wilson in a cozy “den,” created together in our book nook, with popcorn to enjoy as we listen—just like the creatures in the story. Children will design a “bear cave” craft and decorate their dens with natural materials while learning what makes a safe, warm habitat.

events.title: A Play: Walter Cronkite is Dead
events.description: THE STORY : A fierce thunderstorm has shut down airports up and down the East Coast. Two women, who appear to have nothing in common, are stuck in a waiting area at Reagan National Airport. Patty is a chatty southerner—a blue-collar woman from a red state—who is almost physically unable to tolerate silence. Margaret is a Washingtonian, reserved, educated, liberal and not interested in sharing her thoughts, or her table, with Patty. Forced together for a long night in a public place, the two strangers have no choice but to share a bottle of wine and begin to talk...and to listen. Their conversation is funny, difficult, deeply revealing and astonishingly frank. Patty and Margaret share details of their lives that lead them to a place of kinship neither of them could have imagined. Yes, Walter Cronkite is dead, but his wisdom and compassion lives on in this insightful comedy about what might be possible if people from opposite sides of the political aisle would stop shouting and take even one night to listen.

events.title: The Initials Game Live
events.description: Wednesdays at Duluth Cider come try the new hit bar trivia game, The Initials Game Live, made famous on KFAN radio! The Initials Game Live is a fun and competitive general knowledge and pop culture party game for players of all skill levels. Gather your friends and test your wits as you try to guess the initials of famous people, places, and things. It's FREE! There’s no cost to play, and tons of great prizes for the winners (we even have prizes for non-winners!) HOW TO PLAY: 1. Gather your friends - Bring a crew of your favorite companions to the nearest Initials Game Live location. 2. Listen to the clues - You’ll hear six clues per item. They start out tricky, but don’t worry! They get progressively easier. 3. Submit your guess - The sooner you submit the correct answer, the more points you get. If you guess wrong, you’re out until the next item. 4. Tally them up! - Each round contains five items. A full game consists of three rounds. Prizes awarded at the end of each round!

events.description: Celebrate community, greenery, and good food at the Discovery Center and Minocqua Public Library's Plant Swap and Potluck! events.title: Canning 101 with Marsha Fairfield
events.description: Learn the ins and outs of canning food for preservation purposes! In this workshop participants will learn how to preserve food by using both water bath and pressure canning processes. Discussions will include which process to use and why, canning and food safety, and basic recipes to try at home. Marsha Fairfield has been canning for over twenty years. She has incorporated a variety of food preservation techniques while stocking her pantry over the years. Participants will have several opportunities to participate in both techniques using a variety of vegetables. All materials will be provided. No experience necessary! Space is limited and registration is required by 10/27/2026. $65/Member and $75/Non-Member. Thursday, October 29th, 9:00 AM - 4:00 PM. events.description: Admission $12.00 Location NLDC Lodge or Amphitheater Description Wherever you are in your yoga practice, this class is for you. events.title: Soldiers of the American Revolution - Gilbert VFW, hosted by Gilbert Public Library
events.description: The Arrowhead Library System is pleased to present Soldiers of the American Revolution with Arn Kind of Historical Experiences. These free history events will travel to participating ALS libraries October 14-November 20, 2026. On this 250th Anniversary of the Declaration of Independence join Arn Kind for an event all about the American Revolution. This in depth presentation puts audience members into the life of a revolutionary soldier with historical artifacts, uniforms, and hands-on experiences. Audiences will enjoy learning about the causes of the revolution and how it led to the birth of the United States of America. This two hour program is suited for ages 10 and up. events.title: Cataloging Workday
events.description: Cataloging Workday Tuesday, November 24, 2026 – 10:00 to3:00 In Person at ALS Audience: Horizon and BLUEcloud Catalogers with questions Description: ALS catalogers assemble to offer expertise and advice during a day of work! This session will focus on special topics and questions staff have about any aspect of cataloging, brainstorming common issues, and some discussion of cataloging standards across the ALS system. We will be working on cataloging items, so bring up to 15 items and questions to go with them. We suggest bringing a few special items like kits or "library of things" items to discuss, and there will be access to OCLC records. There will be a half hour brown bag lunch/break at noon, and attendees can come and go as they please. Note: if possible, please bring any laptops or relevant tech to help you work. In order to address issues equitably, please only bring up to 15 examples you’d like us to work on.

events.title: Music Then and Now Concert: Coleraine Public Library
events.description: Free Solo String Concerts to tour local ALS libraries this November and December The Arrowhead Library System is pleased to present free concerts at participating ALS libraries November 17 - December 18, 2026. This music event, presented by musician Sara Pajunen, is titled: Music Then and Now: a Solo String Concert . Join Sara Pajunen on a tour of classical, folk, and original music on violin and hardanger d'amore, a ten-string bow instrument. This concert showcases Sara's musical repertoire and original compositions, inspired by travels abroad and grounded in her childhood on the Iron Range. This program is 50 minutes long and suited for adults and children of all ages. These free programs are being offered at the following locations: Tuesday, November 17, 1:00 p.m. - Ely Public Library Wednesday, November 18, 6:30 p.m. - International Falls Public Library Thursday, November 19, 10:00 a.m. - CHI Lakewood Care Center, hosted by Baudette Public Library Friday, November 20, 10:00 a.m. - Mountain Iron Public Library Friday, November 20, 3:30 p.m. - Buhl Public Library Saturday, November 21, 10:00 a.m. - Eveleth Public Library Wednesday, December 2, 10:00 a.m.

events.title: Humbletown Live at Lake Wind Coffee
events.description: Humbletown's coming to the North Woods!! They will be playing a donation-based Monday matinee show at Lake Wind Coffee. Formed in the humble prairie town of Vermillion, South Dakota, Humbletown has emerged as a powerful multi-genre bluegrass-inspired ensemble. Now based out of the Black Hills, the band is inspired by the quiet beauty of pine-filled forests, with original songs inspired by their home and travels, intricately performed on clawhammer banjo, flatpick guitar, and upright bass. With music that combines influences of bluegrass, old time, hot club swing, Americana, and classic country, Humbletown will take you on a musical journey that stretches across time and space. Their 2022 debut album “The Path I Chose to Walk” received international acclaim. Americana UK’s review described the album: “The first impression on listening to these songs around virtuosos on clawhammer banjo and flat-picking guitar is that this entire collection must have been something discovered nearly a century ago by the great ethnomusicologist Alan Lomax.”

events.title: Full Moon Monday at Sir Ben's with Teague Alexy and friends
events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: Teague Alexy continues his Monday residency at Sir Ben's in Duluth, MN. There will be special guests to celebrate the full moon. Teague's new album EFFERVESCENT is now streaming. Award-winning Duluth-based musician, author and storyteller Teague Alexy is probably best known for his Americana songwriting in the national touring brothers duo Hobo Nephews of Uncle Frank. Teague’s songwriting is clearly influenced by his home in Minnesota, as well as his childhood in New Jersey, and life as a travelling musical hobo. Teague's storytelling has deeper roots to his Irish ancestry. The name ‘Teague’ was once used to describe the storytelling poets who travelled ancient Ireland. New album "Effervescent" available 2/14/16. Teague's second album of 2017 is a collaboration with Trampled By Turtles mandolin player Erik Berry. 'Irish American' features nine traditional Irish favorites, including "Whiskey in the Jar," "The Wild Colonial Boy" and "Mountain Dew," as well as two original songs.

events.title: Max Subar
events.description: Max Subar and Minor Moon Fall Duo Tour. DM for address Chicago singer-songwriter Max Subar joins the Merge Records roster with his debut full-length album "Anything Could Be." Laid down on a mobile recording rig in a house on the shore of a frozen lake in Wisconsin, Max emerged after ten days of solitude with a record of neither fallow nor verdant earth, but, staggeringly, one that occupies the threshold between the two, a space that accommodates the potential for stagnation and growth: their hopes, their worries, the time it takes to arrive at an unknown destination, and the courage to accept what’s there, waiting to be realized. “There is so much room for newness in the weightiest or seemingly most paralyzing of times,” Subar explains. “No matter how foreign, frightening, anxiety-ridden, or unfamiliar chapters of life can feel, there is always an opportunity to tap deep into ourselves and land somewhere new, somewhere forward.”

events.title: Minor Moon
events.description: house show, dm for address :: https://www.instagram.com/inclinestares/ Max Subar (duo) Minor Moon (duo) Kara Warren Minor Moon, The Light Up Waltz Out via Ruination Record Co., April 12th, 2024 At the heart of Minor Moon’s open-ended and knotty country rock songs is an undeniably inviting lightness. While the Chicago-based songwriter and bandleader Sam Cantor writes impressionistic songs about the end of the world, they’re wrapped in such a warm blanket of lush guitars and pastoral twang that they always leave a hopeful spark. On their latest LP, The Light Up Waltz, Cantor sings of the fantastical in magical traveling bands, swaying bridges, and aquamarine metamorphoses. Still, he’s concerned with fundamentally human questions about who we are and how we reinvent ourselves when everything crumbles around us. While the 2021 release of Minor Moon’s third LP Tethers coincided with a transitional period in Cantor’s life, The Light Up Waltz materialized during a time of unprecedented personal stability and creativity. He immersed himself in Chicago’s immensely collaborative music community performing live with V.V. Lightbody, Andrew Sa, Half Gringa, and more.

events.title: Zach Williams
events.description: Music is meant to feel “lived-in,” not unlike a favorite old jacket or a first car. At least that’s what multiplatinum two-time GRAMMY® Award-winning Arkansas-born and Nashville-based maverick Zach Williams would say. Through a fusion of southern rock spirit and country soul, Zach creates music with an exterior which is worn down in the best way, but all heart underneath rough guitar riffs and gravelly vocals. You’ll not only hear his journey in the music, but you’ll also see it in his unfiltered storytelling—how he went from a tiny town to international stardom, selling out shows, toppling charts, and collaborating with the likes of Dolly Parton. Along the way, he battled addiction, anxiety, and insecurity, coming out on the other side with a whole lot to say. After living through the lowest of lows and the highest of highs, he made a choice to trust his gut more than ever in 2021. Doing so had certainly served him well up to this point, so he wholeheartedly embraced his most formative inspirations, including rock and old school country.

events.title: Nu-Blu Bluegrass Artists
events.description: Nu-Blu, based in Siler City in central North Carolina, is comprised of Carolyn Routh, who handles bass and vocals; Austin Hefflefinger on vocals and banjo; Justin Harrison, on mandolin and fiddle; and Daniel Routh, who is the band’s Renaissance Man – guitarist, singer, manager, and tour coordinator, among many other roles. The group brings its lively and entertaining version of Americana-bluegrass music to audiences across the nation year-round. Their sound acknowledges the traditional institutions that have shaped it, yet is innovative and daring enough to bring a fresh sparkle to contemporary acoustic music that lands them squarely in the forefront of bands blazing the trail in acoustic entertainment. Influences range from the sounds of original bluegrass pioneers like Earl Scruggs, Jimmy Martin and Lester Flatt to rock bands of the 1980’s, and modern contemporary sounds such as Alison Krauss and Union Station. Carolyn’s soprano vocal approach might be described as similar to Ms. Krauss, except she carries a phrasing and emotional elegance that shows a clear originality.

events.title: Indecent Proposal
events.description: Sip & Serenade is back at Jack’s Place for a special edition night featuring Indecent Proposal’s lead guitarist, Jason Owen. Jason takes classic songs and flips them with his own twist — smooth grooves, sharp turns, and those little “wait... run that back” moments that catch the whole room at once. It’s the perfect kind of midweek reset: laid-back enough to hang, but the guitar work keeps you locked in. Bring your crew, grab a drink, and let Wednesday night get a little indecent. come out and get Indecent 😈😎🎸🤘💜 www.indyp218.com Indecent Proposal is a band out of Duluth, Minnesota, built around connection, feel, and songs that hold up in a room full of people. Blending modern alt-rock, groove-driven covers, and emotionally grounded originals, the band focuses on moments you can feel as much as hear. Their live shows move fluidly between intimacy and release—quiet verses, loud hearts, and choruses that come back at you from the crowd. Led by frontman Josh Brown, with Selie’s dynamic vocals, Jason Soderlund on guitar, Terry Beckman on bass, and Andy Fabian on drums, Indecent Proposal brings intention to every set and honesty to every song.

events.title: Ian Alexy
events.description: Troubadour 21st Century is the new record by singer-songwriter Ian Alexy. Best known for his work with Americana duo Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank, Ian expands the possibilities on Troubadour 21st Century with rock grooves and spine-tingling electric guitar flourishes. This is Ian Alexy’s fifth album as a solo artist, in addition to five albums with Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank. Hobo Nephews first earned their live reputation by opening a sold-out national tour for Trampled By Turtles before touring all over the United States as a headliner. Their 2015 song Old Number 4 was featured on CBS Sports.com and soon after went viral. Ian has received critical acclaim for his work as a solo artist as well. In addition to performing as a solo artist and with his band Ian Alexy and The Deserters, he is also working on a series of documentaries titled Making It Shine comprised of footage of life on the road and in the studio over the past several years. With the world re opening again the Troubadour 21st Century is ready to return to the music life. “Invokes 80s era Petty and Springsteen.” - Minneapolis Star Tribune “Stomping Blues Rock reminiscent of Dan Auerbach.”

events.title: 38 Special
events.description: After more than four decades together, 38 SPECIAL continues to bring their signature blast of Southern Rock to over 100 cities a year. And at each and every show, thousands of audience members are amazed by the explosive power of the band's performance. Their many Gold and Platinum album awards stand in testament to the endurance of a legendary powerhouse. With sales in excess of 20 million, most associate the band with their arena-rock pop smashes, “Hold On Loosely,” “Rockin’ Into the Night,” “Caught Up in You,” “Fantasy Girl,” “If I’d Been the One,” “Back Where You Belong,” “Chain Lightnin’,” “Second Chance,” and more – Timeless hits that remain a staple at radio, immediately recognizable from the first opening chord, and paving the way to their present-day touring regimen.

events.title: 38 Special
events.description: 38 Special is an American rock band. Formed by Guitarist/Vocalist Don Barnes and vocalist Donnie Van Zant in 1974 in Jacksonville, Florida, the band initially had a straight-ahead Southern rock sound, much like Lynyrd Skynyrd, the band of Donnie's older brother Ronnie. By the early 1980s, the band began incorporating elements of blues-rock and arena rock into their sound, kicking off a string of successful albums and singles. Among 38 Special's best-known songs are "Caught Up in You" (1982) and "If I'd Been the One" (1983), both of which hit #1 on Billboard magazine's album rock chart, and "Second Chance" (1989), a #1 hit on Billboard's adult contemporary chart. Their other hit singles include "Hold On Loosely" (1981) and "Back Where You Belong" (1984). The band is comprised of guitarist/vocalist Don Barnes, guitarist Jerry Riggs, bassist Barry Dunaway, keyboardist Bobby Capps, and drummer Gary Moffatt.

events.description: The six men comprising STYX have committed to rocking the Paradise together with audiences far and wide by averaging over 100 shows a year every year since (yes) 1999, and each one of them is committed to making the next show better than the last. Founded in Chicago in 1972, STYX has the unique distinction of being the first band in rock history to have four consecutive certified multimillion-selling albums in a row: 1977’s The Grand Illusion, 1978’s Pieces of Eight, 1979’s Cornerstone, and 1981’s Paradise Theatre. STYX draws from over four decades of barnburning chart hits, joyous singalongs, and harddriving deep cuts. Like a symphony that builds to a satisfying crescendo, a STYX set covers a wide range of stylistic cornerstones.

events.title: Amy Speace
events.description: A tour celebrating the launch of Amy's debut book of poetry, "The Cardinals" (Red Hen Press). She will be singing and reading selections from the book, which will be on sale at the show. Heralded by Rolling Stone, Billboard Magazine and The New York Times and featured on NPR’s “All Things Considered”, Amy Speace was discovered by Judy Collins, who signed her to her record label and has recorded her songs. She’s the 2020 winner of the AMA UK’s International Song of the Year. Her newest record, “The American Dream,” was released October 18th and became the #1 record and the title track was named #1 song in the FAI Radio Charts for its first month out. Her song, “The Weight of the World” was named the #4 record of last decade by WFUV, NYC. As well, her song, “The Sea and the Shore” was named as one of the 100 best folk songs of the era. She will be releasing a single of Woody Guthrie’s “Plane Wreck at Los Gatos” this summer accompanied by a video, to help raise awareness for the ACLU. A writer’s writer, her forthcoming debut collection of poetry will be published by Red Hen Press in Spring 2027.

events.title: Styx
events.description: Tommy Shaw, James “JY” Young, Lawrence Gowan, Todd Sucherman, Will Evankovich, and Terry Gowan (along with the occasional surprise appearance by original bassist Chuck Panozzo), have performed more live since ’99 than all of the previous years of its career combined. Two Super-Bowl appearances, Pollstar Box Office chart-topping tours with Def Leppard, Journey, Boston, REO Speedwagon, Bad Company (to name only a few), two more studio albums and no end in sight, STYX continues to conquer the planet, one venue at a time. Spawned from a suburban Chicago basement in the early ‘70s, Styx would eventually transform into the virtual arena rock prototype by the late '70s and early '80s, due to a fondness for big rockers and soaring power ballads. Early on, Styx's music reflected such then-current prog rockers as Emerson, Lake & Palmer and the Moody Blues, as evidenced by such releases as 1972's self-titled debut, 1973's Styx II, 1974's The Serpent Is Rising, and 1975's Man of Miracles.

events.description: This summer, Jen and Kristin from #IMOMSOHARD are taking their show out of the playroom and onto the road. But this time, they’re bringing the kids. And a tour bus (you didn’t think they’d leave them with their husbands, did you?). There’s no one making moms feel as uncomfortably normal as Kristin Hensley and Jen Smedley, the hilarious oh-so-real women behind #IMomSoHard. With over 675,000 Facebook fans, and more than 55 million views of their web series, Jen and Kristin’s blend of honesty and humor offer the kinds of levity most of us only get from our therapist, proving that if we weren’t all laughing, we’d be crying, right? Right!? Sure to deliver the kind of straight talk you can only get from discussing body hair in the kids’ playroom while sipping mimosas, Kristin and Jen prove you can’t make this shi*t up. It’s like an evening with two of your besties. But funnier. And probably with more drinking.

She and the fellas struck thick, dusty groove and a hazy-cool vibe on their new seven-song mini album, "In It to Win It," which includes a heart-tugging Nick Lowe cover and an instant road-trip classic called "Idle Down."” - Chris Riemenschneider — Minneapolis Star Tribune Late-blooming Minnesota singer-songwriter Becky Kapell writes gritty, no-nonsense songs that come from the crossroads of old-time rock and roll and country. events.title: Gary Owen
events.description: Gary Owen has been entertaining audiences for more than two decades with his sharp observational humor and fearless storytelling. Known for his unapologetic, rule-defying style, his material draws from his personal life, time in the military and the everyday absurdities that connect people across backgrounds. With a fanbase that has grown by the millions in recent months and continues to surge across social media, Owen’s reach has cemented his place as one of the most in-demand touring comedians today. Beyond stand-up, Owen has appeared in a wide range of feature films including BACK ON THE STRIP with Tiffany Haddish and Wesley Snipes, MEET THE BLACKS and its sequel THE HOUSE NEXT DOOR, THINK LIKE A MAN and THINK LIKE A MAN TOO, RIDE ALONG with Ice Cube and Kevin Hart, LITTLE MAN opposite the Wayans Brothers, and DADDY DAY CARE with Eddie Murphy. He is also widely recognized for his scene-stealing role as “Bearcat” in the MGM film COLLEGE. On television, Owen starred in his own BET series THE GARY OWEN SHOW and co-hosted TruTV’s sketch series UPLOAD WITH SHAQUILLE O’NEAL.

events.title: John Louis
events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: Country troubadour John Louis wanders around this world of music, writing and singing heartworn country folk songs. John’s that guy on the bus who sits quietly, looking tired like the rest of us. The difference is he is sitting there composing a song about your life and those painful poignant moments you dust off on the way home between life’s chores. His songs show us our lives and the subtle but important things that become universally important hallmarks of our Midwestern journey. Like church basement rolls at the funeral. Like the small moments on road trips filled with meaning, loss and memory. The tragedies and triumphs that break us and keep us going one more day. John glimpses it all through a poet’s heart. When he stands bravely on a stage with a guitar and begins singing, we get to see it too. And it makes sense for a moment. The songs John writes keep winning awards from prestigious songwriting showcases. Including the Kerrville Folk Festival New Folk competition, Rocky Mountain Folks Festival Songwriter Showcase, and the Great River Folk Fest songwriter contest. (That’s some hot sh-t folks!)

Smith's first full-length work, "Flowers," releases on Nov. 6. Both will have vinyl (and CD's) available. Sampaguita is one of Smith's most beloved hometown venues. A 'third place" (all are welcome) that celebrates original art in all it's forms. This will be an intimate, seated show. events.title: The Oak Ridge Boys
events.description: Theirs has been one of the most distinctive and timeless sounds in the music industry for over 50 years, and now The Oak Ridge Boys are bringing their Celebrating Route 66 tour across the country for an unforgettable night of entertainment for the entire family. The show will feature many of the group's country hits and two pop smashes, songs that earned them Grammy, Dove, CMA, and ACM awards, as well as garnering a host of other industry and fan accolades. "When I go on stage, I get the same feeling I had the first time I sang with The Oak Ridge Boys," says lead singer Duane Allen. "This is the only job I've ever wanted to have." "'Elvira' was always on repeat when I was growing up," says tenor Ben James. "It's still one of those timeless songs that never grow old." James first met The Oak Ridge Boys in November 2022. "Joe (Bonsall) handed me the mic and said, 'You've got the next verse,'" James said. "I'm not sure I will ever get over that moment." A little more than a year later, Bonsall handed the microphone to James permanently, announcing his retirement from the group in January of 2024. Bonsall passed away several months later due to complications from ALS.

events.title: Teague Alexy
events.description: Nicholas David and Teague Alexy make their Grand Rapids debut as a duo. Nicholas and Teague aka Teague and The Feelin collaborated on the acclaimed 2006 album The New Folklore. Award-winning Duluth-based musician, author and storyteller Teague Alexy is probably best known for his Americana songwriting in the national touring brothers duo Hobo Nephews of Uncle Frank. Teague’s songwriting is clearly influenced by his home in Minnesota, as well as his childhood in New Jersey, and life as a travelling musical hobo. Teague's storytelling has deeper roots to his Irish ancestry. The name ‘Teague’ was once used to describe the storytelling poets who travelled ancient Ireland. New album "Effervescent" available 2/14/16. Teague's second album of 2017 is a collaboration with Trampled By Turtles mandolin player Erik Berry. 'Irish American' features nine traditional Irish favorites, including "Whiskey in the Jar," "The Wild Colonial Boy" and "Mountain Dew," as well as two original songs.

events.description: Barron Ryan’s love for music has always been divided. The son of two musicians, he grew up in a house filled with the sounds of everything ranging from Beethoven to James Brown. So when it comes to his own performing, he’s not content drawing on just one of those influences; he combines them all into an adventure that’s vintage yet fresh, historical yet hip, classic yet cool. Even when beginning to make his own music, Barron needed more than one outlet. He started piano lessons at the age of four, but at the same time began teaching himself drums. While progressing through middle and high schools, he won prizes in classical piano competitions while also earning a reputation as a formidable jazz drummer. In college, Barron continued to excel in multiple fields, majoring in piano performance and even earning a spot playing snare in the marching band drumline. Though he increasingly turned his focus toward the piano, the genres of classical, jazz, and funk continued to attract his attention. Now Barron applies his myriad interests and expertise to create an awe-inspiring program.

Grab your crew, settle in, and spend the night with us at Mr. D’s. Come out and get Indecent 😈😎🎸🤘💜 www.indyp218.com Indecent Proposal is a band out of Duluth, Minnesota, built around connection, feel, and songs that hold up in a room full of people. Blending modern alt-rock, groove-driven covers, and emotionally grounded originals, the band focuses on moments you can feel as much as hear. Their live shows move fluidly between intimacy and release—quiet verses, loud hearts, and choruses that come back at you from the crowd. Led by frontman Josh Brown, with Selie’s dynamic vocals, Jason Soderlund on guitar, Terry Beckman on bass, and Andy Fabian on drums, Indecent Proposal brings intention to every set and honesty to every song. Whether it’s an original like Glow, The Cage, or Drift Away, or a re-imagined cover, the goal is the same: make the room feel something together.

events.title: Shane Nelson - Havannas (Superior WI)
events.description: Live music with songwriter Shane Nelson -grab some authentic Cubin food, a drink and a seat, and enjoy an evening of listening. Shane Nelson is a singer, songwriter, musician, and producer who has been following his artistic instincts to create since he was a child. Nelson started performing at school and community events when he was 8 years old. In his teens, Nelson built the band, “Crescent Moon”. Along with his band, Shane has earned recognition as one of the Northland’s top local musical acts by winning several battle of the bands competitions, being voted the Northland’s best live musical act by local radio stations, and through live performances throughout the Midwest. Nelson’s band has performed alongside nationally recognized acts such as Survivor, Toad the Wet Sprocket, and Confederate Railroad. As a solo artist, Shane has been featured on PBS television, has won several singer/songwriter contests, and earned the title of Northland Idol through a local ABC Television affiliate which landed him in Nashville, TN. Although Nelson has won several awards and has received recognition for his musical abilities, he is not in it for the eminence.

events.title: Mason Jennings
events.description: Mason Jennings is a Minnesota-based pop-folk singer-songwriter. Jennings is originally from Honolulu, Hawaii. He is well known for his simple yet catchy melodies, intimate lyrics, intensely literary and historical themes, and deep tenor's voice. His music has appeared in the surf film Shelter and he has toured extensively. Jennings is married to Amy Jennings (nee Turany) and has a son, August, born in January 2003. Jennings produced his self-titled debut album in 1997 on an analog four-track in the basement of a rented home, manning all instruments himself. In October 1998, after bringing drummer Chris Stock and bassist Robert Skoro on board, he began a weekly gig at Minneapolis' 400 Bar as the Mason Jennings Band. Garnering local praise and a wide fan base, Mason began touring nationally. His 2000 album Birds Flying Away revealed Jennings' political activism and penchant for singing first-person narratives of imaginary rustic characters. Following the release of this album, Noah Levy took over drumming duties from Stock. 2002 saw the release of two albums: the studio piece Century Spring and a "fans only" collection of acoustic rarities, Simple Life.

events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: Country troubadour John Louis wanders around this world of music, writing and singing heartworn country folk songs. John’s that guy on the bus who sits quietly, looking tired like the rest of us. The difference is he is sitting there composing a song about your life and those painful poignant moments you dust off on the way home between life’s chores. His songs show us our lives and the subtle but important things that become universally important hallmarks of our Midwestern journey. Like church basement rolls at the funeral. Like the small moments on road trips filled with meaning, loss and memory. The tragedies and triumphs that break us and keep us going one more day. John glimpses it all through a poet’s heart. When he stands bravely on a stage with a guitar and begins singing, we get to see it too. And it makes sense for a moment. The songs John writes keep winning awards from prestigious songwriting showcases. Including the Kerrville Folk Festival New Folk competition, Rocky Mountain Folks Festival Songwriter Showcase, and the Great River Folk Fest songwriter contest. (That’s some hot sh-t folks!)

For a band on the road, 20 years can be more than a lifetime. Yet, after 2 decades of making music together in living rooms, listening rooms, clubs, theaters, and festival stages, The Steel Wheels are still growing, still pushing, still at it, and they’re marking the occasion with the release of their 9th studio album, “The Steel Wheels”. Following the release of “Sideways” in 2024, their 3rd record with producer Sam Kassirer at his Great North Sound Society studio in interior Maine, the band felt it was time for a change of scene. As the group began to select songs for a new album, they also had to find an answer to the question of where they would get down to the work of record-making. They didn’t know that answer was going to knock on their back door. events.title: The New Standards Holiday Show ~ Duluth, MN
events.description: The New Standards Holiday Show features the trio as wise-cracking hosts of a seasonal spectacle that's just Christmasy enough. With a little help from their friends, The New Standards warms the hearts of the grinchiest of grinches in what has become an enduring, and endearing, Minnesota holiday tradition. Minnesota stalwarts The New Standards create an intriguing blend of everything from classic cabaret to punk rock, from the freedom of jazz, to the soul of pop and rock. They make it work through sheer musicianship and offbeat humor. The instrumentation is simple: John Munson of Trip Shakespeare/Semisonic fame on bass; Chan Poling, founder of the new-wave group The Suburbs on piano; and Steve Roehm on vibes. Chan and John split the singing. A foot stomp here, a shout-out, a fiery solo, and it's cooked. Simple, elegant, illuminating.

events.description: Davina and the Vagabonds bring a signature high-energy blend of blues, neo-soul, and swing to the winter season with their annual "A Vagabond Holiday" shows and festive recordings. Known for frontwoman Davina Sowers' distinctively soulful vocals and a heavy brass presence, the Twin Cities-based group frequently hits the road each winter. New Spin on an Old Sound Davina and the Vagabonds are playing your area soon! Davina Sowers and the Vagabonds have created a stir on the national music scene with their high-energy live shows, level A musicianship, sharp-dressed professionalism, and Sowers’ commanding stage presence. With influences ranging from Fats Domino and the Preservation Hall Jazz Band to Aretha Franklin and Tom Waits, the band is converting audiences one show at a time, from Vancouver to Miami and across Europe. In 2011 Davina released her first full length, all original album Black Cloud . It was named one of the 10 best releases of the year by the Minneapolis Star & Tribune and awarded 4 1⁄2 stars from Downbeat Magazine.

events.description: The Event Center, Floodwood GB Leighton acoustic show The Event Center, Floodwood 201 West 7th Avenue Floodwood, MN 55736 More than 200 shows a year. Jubilant fans who follow him from Minnesota to Mexico. More than 100,000 albums sold. A new release “Get Up” and a state-of-the-art nightclub named after one of his songs -- all without the support of a major record label... Meet GB Leighton, a band named after one of the regions’ most incendiary live performers and consistently solid songwriters, Brian Leighton. Through more than a decade and eleven studio albums, Leighton and his five piece band have been tearing up rock clubs, festivals and even a few fan’s living rooms with a slew of songs that connect with the heart and couples singing along out on the dance floor. “A man of the people” is a phrase usually reserved for statesmen and politicians, but for Leighton, it’s a fitting description when you see him in action working a crowd. Leighton delivers that same inescapable rock ‘n’ roll spirit night after night. “If I hadn’t heard a bunch of Bruce’s bootlegs or seen the videos I’d be a much different musician,” he says today.

events.title: An Irish Christmas with Rend Collective - Duluth
events.description: Hailing from the rugged coast of Northern Ireland, Rend Collective has always believed that worship should feel more like a celebration than a performance. From their earliest days gathering on beaches and in living rooms to now leading worship across the world, the band has held tightly to one mission: to joyfully share the good news of Jesus through authentic, Spirit-filled worship. Since the release of their debut Organic Family Hymnal, Rend Collective has grown from a small worshipping community into a global voice, amassing over 1 billion career streams, and multiple gold and platinum selling singles, including fan favorites like “My Lighthouse,” “Counting Every Blessing,” and “Build Your Kingdom Here.” Their catalog also includes the international worship anthem “Hallelujah Anyway,” which has resonated deeply with churches around the world. The group’s breakout single “Build Your Kingdom Here” became an early global anthem, and their momentum carried into a historic run of chart-topping albums. The Art of Celebration debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard Christian Albums Chart, followed by several additional No. 1 records including As Family We Go, Good News, and Campfire.

events.description: Celebrating 22 years in 2026! Get ready for the Rock & Roll Xmas Spectacular, where your favorite holiday classics collide with iconic rock anthems in a high-energy show with enough confetti to make Rudolph blush! Join an all-star lineup featuring Paul "Stretch" Diethelm and Ted Manderfeld, alongside powerhouse vocalists Pamela McNeill, Stacy Bauer, and Tim Haussner. They'll be backed by an incredible band including bassist Cody McKinney, saxophonist and flutist Mike Kreitzer, and drummer Pete Hennig. events.description: Andrew Crowley on the piano Andrew Crowley is a Twin Cities-based musician, composer, and audio engineer with a dynamic career spanning from major label rock stages to the baseball diamond. events.title: Jay Webb
events.description: Country artist Jay Webb writes songs that hit like a gut punch. Raised between the backroads of North Alabama and the city in the south, music was how he made sense of the chaos around him. What started as a way to process a turbulent childhood quickly became his purpose — gritty storytelling over genre-blurring beats, delivered with zero filter. He started cutting demos in high school and never stopped, releasing track after track on his own and building a following from the ground up. His lyrics cut deep, his voice carries the scars and his sound refuses to stay in one lane. Webb doesn’t clean up the mess — he leans into it, and has a good time doing it. Pulling from a wide range of influences, he pairs the weight of Johnny Cash and Hank Williams with the edge of Juice WRLD and Post Malone. It’s not traditional country — and he doesn’t want it to be. He calls it “music for real people with real problems,” and his fans know exactly what that means. In 2022, a viral TikTok pushed his music to a wider audience. Since then, he’s dropped standout tracks like “Down Here,” “Bury Me With Bourbon” and “Broken,” racking up over 415M streams and more than 2M fans.

events.title: Mitchell Tenpenny
events.description: Six years into his record deal with Columbia Records, Mitchell Tenpenny is leaning in even more. On his new album “The 3rd,” the Nashville native is leaning into his story, his fans, his roots and his influences – all with an eye on the future. Country radio knows Tenpenny as a reliable hitmaker and husky-voiced storyteller with an ear for undeniable hooks and unforgettable melodies. Fans who care to listen deeper recognize that he not only produces country radio smashes but is also a genre disruptor unafraid of punctuating his country storytelling with edgy lyrics, hard-driving drum beats and heavy guitars. “The 3rd” is Tenpenny’s most authentic – and adventurous – album yet. Named after a song that was named after him, “The 3rd” is a testament to his personal growth and artistic evolution. No longer playing games, Tenpenny has crafted an album that resonates with his own experiences and emotions. This honest and empathetic collection showcases his maturity as a man, singer, songwriter, and storyteller and invites listeners to join him on his creative journey through life and music. “I want this record to be all over the place,” Tenpenny said.

events.title: Flo Rida
events.description: Tramar Dillard [born December 16th 1979], better known by the stage name of Flo Rida, is an American rapper. He was born in Opa-locka, Florida but raised in Carol City, and chose his name from his home state. As a teenager, he toured with local rap group 2 Live Crew. Later, he appeared in numerous popular rap mixtapes, most notably in 'We The Best' by DJ Khaled in 2006, when he was signed to the Poe Boy Entertainment label, distributed by Atlantic Records. 'Mail On Sunday' is the debut album by the American hip hop artist Flo Rida. Flo Rida explained the versatility of the album with the following, "I cover everything from hardships to struggle to the good times at the club. I got a song called 'Freaky,' I got party music, I got something for the car. I got all different types of music". Flo Rida also elaborated on the title of the album stating, "Well, this record is like my special delivery for the fans. Itâ€TMs not something you can get during the 6 regular mail delivery days. You need that extra day for your prized possessions. Thatâ€TMs Mail on Sunday." The album debuted at No.3 on the U.S. Billboard 200 chart, selling 85,891 copies in its first week.

Their debut album, the self-titled Daughtry, was the top-selling album of 2007 and was the fastest selling rock debut album in Soundscan history. The record was nominated for 4 GRAMMY® Awards and won 4 American Music Awards, alongside 7 Billboard Music Awards, including “Album of the Year.” Subsequent albums, Leave This Town (2009), Break The Spell (2011), and Baptized (2013) have all gone Platinum, with Cage To Rattle (2018) certified Gold. events.title: Comedy Night with Johnny Beehner
events.description: With a background in improvisational theater, including training at Chicago’s prestigious Second City and the Upright Citizens Brigade in Los Angeles, Johnny brings a very unique style to the stage. He made his network television debut in January of 2015 as one of the last comedians to appear on the Late Show with David Letterman. He has also made numerous appearances on FOX’s Laughs, has appeared on AXS’s Gotham Comedy Live, and regularly appears on the nationally syndicated Bob & Tom Show. His comedy can be heard regularly on XM/ Sirius Satellite radio.

events.title: Guys On Ice
events.description: Grab your thermos, drill a hole in the ice, and settle in for the hilarious musical comedy about friendship, fishing, and frozen winters. The Quintessential Comedy of the North From the land of ten thousand lakes to the frozen bays of the Great Lakes, Guys on Ice is hitting the road to celebrate the secret language of the North: ice fishing. This beloved musical comedy invites audiences into a world where the beer is cold, the stove is warm, and the wisdom is as thick as the ice on the lake. More than just a play, Guys on Ice is a musical tribute to the stubborn resilience of Midwesterners. Featuring show-stopping numbers like "De Wishing Hole," "Fish is de Miracle Food," and the legendary "Ode to a Snowmobile Suit" (featuring a zipper dance routine you have to see to believe), this production captures the heart, the humor, and the "oh-fer-cute" charm of life on the ice.

events.title: NEEDTOBREATHE
events.description: Despite a 20-year history that includes all the accolades of an iconic band, GRAMMY-nominated, multi-platinum band NEEDTOBREATHE came into their latest studio album with a much different frame of mind. They still felt they had something to prove. In truth, this is a band who have loomed large for years, leveraging a unique fusion of modern rock, purpose-driven soul and irresistible pop appeal into a stat line which puts them in exceedingly rare company. They’ve placed five Number One albums all across the Billboard chart spectrum, from Rock and Alternative. They’ve racked up two billion career streams and scored multi-platinum chart topping hits – “Brother” (feat. Gavin DeGraw), “Who Am I,” “Let’s Stay Home Tonight” and dozens more. And they’ve done it all while filling venues across the globe. Ask their fans and it’s been two decades of spirit-mining songs, master musicianship and elemental artistry, digging deep to create a series of sonic monuments to the human condition. Their most recent effort follows suit.

events.title: NEEDTOBREATHE
events.description: NEEDTOBREATHE has established itself as one of the most dynamic and influential bands in modern rock. Known for their powerful live shows and emotionally resonant songwriting, the band has released a string of critically acclaimed albums, earned multiple GRAMMY nominations, and built a devoted audience around the world. Their music blends rock, Americana, soul, and gospel influences into a sound that is uniquely their own, anchored by songs that speak to perseverance, faith, redemption, and the shared human experience. On November 19, the band is set to release The Long Surrender and The Fellow Passengers of Pain, the deluxe edition of their acclaimed album The Long Surrender.

Ski North Ultra
events.description: Ski North Ultra is an ultra-distance 100K cross-country skiing classic-only event along the North Shore of Lake Superior. The event has 38K and 100K options, following the Norpine, Cascade River State Park and Bally Creek trail systems near Lutsen, MN. This is a unique cross-country ski event. It is classic-skiing only, and will be on a mix of double-track and single-track ski trails. The trails are incredibly beautiful, and also very technical. State park skiing can mean narrow, sharp turns, and the terrain along Lake Superior can mean long, 20-30 minute climbs, and sharp, steep descents. The 100K race uses advanced courses. The 38K stays on intermediate trails, but please consider if this is the right fit for your skill level. This is a tough course. March snow conditions can be varying, and can also be the most wonderful time of year to enjoy skiing. The event is more of an adventure than a race. Come with an open mind and adventurous spirit, and you will have a great day. Start and finish in Cascade River State Park. Glide through birch, fir, cedar and pine forests, with overlooks of Lake Superior.

events.description: Join us for the 41st Annual Cross Country Ski Races at Giants Ridge in Biwabik, Minnesota, on March 6, 2027! Experience three exciting race categories: * Pepsi Challenge 50K Freestyle & Classic * Great River Energy Rush 25K Freestyle & Classic * Giants Ridge 8K Cross Country Ski Race Our family-friendly events welcome skiers of all skill levels. With our no hassle guarantee, you can park, register, stay, race, dine, and relax all in one convenient location. After the race, unwind with a shower, swim and sauna just a short walk away. Giants Ridge offers 60 kilometers of impeccably groomed, world-class Nordic trails, hosting events like the World Cup, Olympic Trials, National Collegiate Finals, U.S. National Championships, and High School Championships. The Pepsi Challenge Cup Race is part of the American Ski Marathon Series and a Birkie Qualifier. Join us on Minnesota's Iron Range for an exciting late-winter cross-country ski experience! We are also seeking volunteers and welcome input from anyone interested in enhancing the quality of our event. Please email pepsichallenge@giantsridge.com with your availability to volunteer or share your feedback.

events.title: Mo Pitney @ The Reif PAC
events.description: When Mo Pitney sings "let me tell you about country" in his debut single, he's doing more than telling. He's showing. Appropriately titled, the song "Country" is as much positioning statement as introduction. In three minutes and 16 seconds, it is almost precisely who he is in word and deed. The vocal delivery, storytelling, musicianship and reflections of his outdoor lifestyle – as well as faith, family and patriotism – offer a spot-on portrayal. Joined by early fan favorites "Clean Up On Aisle Five" and "Come Do A Little Life," the song carves an unmistakably country yet completely fresh groove for the genre. In short, it sounds like nothing else, but absolutely belongs. To paraphrase the song, a life in music isn't a place on a map; it's a place in Mo Pitney's heart. "I just love music," Pitney says, exhibiting atypical maturity for someone still in their early twenties. "It has never been about praise. Playing the Grand Ole Opry was an amazing experience, but I have just as much fun sitting on my bed playing along to an old record. It's always been that way." That music-centered outlook is already generating the unsought acclaim of which he speaks.

Martin Sexton
events.description: America comes together in the music of Martin Sexton. Our hearts mend, our political and philosophical differences melt away, and the various strains of our roots music entangle. Of Sexton, The New York Times says: “His unpretentious heartiness helps him focus on every soul singer’s goal: to amplify the sound of the ordinary heart." Sexton has remained true to his mission of sharing peace and harmony throughout his 10 albums, and in countless incendiary live performances. He has thus built a loyal following of fans, including critics and superstar artists. He is without a doubt what Billboard calls: “The real thing.” These days, people are coming together to revel in Sexton’s musicality for his Martin Sexton Abbey Road Show. This is a live show extravaganza in which he performs the iconic Beatles’ album in its entirety followed by a set of mainly original music. Sexton is a songwriter’s songwriter, with a multi-octave voice that knows no bounds. Acoustic Guitar Magazine calls him a: "Master of dynamics, reducing a room to silence with his blustering baritone, then teasing that silence with a fluttering falsetto."

events.title: Buck Rut Run
events.description: Thank to everyone that has registered so far! We have exceeded our goal! If you haven't registered yet, you still can, however we want to make you aware that as of 8:00 AM on October 23, we are out of t-shirts and we are unable to do a re-order. The Buck Rut Run returns to Minocqua Winter Park for its 31st edition! Will this be the last? The Buck Rut Run celebrated it's 30th edition last year. For the past 5 years we have hovered around 35 participants, with a goal of 50 each year. In 2025 we hit 43, still short of our goal. This event raises money for Minocqua Winter Park and the Lakeland Union High School Cross Country Team. No fee is charged by the timer and all proceeds are divided between these two organizations. The decision has been made by the race organizers that from this point forward, a race that doesn't have at least 50 entries will be the last Buck Rut Run. 2026 IS HAPPENING, 2027 is up to you and your friends! This is a 5K trail run which utilizes the trail system at Minocqua Winter Park. Here is the COURSE MAP (https://runsignup.com/Race/Photos/WI/Minocqua/BuckRutRun) . Online Registration is open from midnight, September 1 to 11:59 PM on October 24.

events.title: Humbletown Live at Lake Wind Coffee
events.description: Humbletown's coming to the North Woods!! They will be playing a donation-based Monday matinee show at Lake Wind Coffee. Formed in the humble prairie town of Vermillion, South Dakota, Humbletown has emerged as a powerful multi-genre bluegrass-inspired ensemble. Now based out of the Black Hills, the band is inspired by the quiet beauty of pine-filled forests, with original songs inspired by their home and travels, intricately performed on clawhammer banjo, flatpick guitar, and upright bass. With music that combines influences of bluegrass, old time, hot club swing, Americana, and classic country, Humbletown will take you on a musical journey that stretches across time and space. Their 2022 debut album “The Path I Chose to Walk” received international acclaim. Americana UK’s review described the album: “The first impression on listening to these songs around virtuosos on clawhammer banjo and flat-picking guitar is that this entire collection must have been something discovered nearly a century ago by the great ethnomusicologist Alan Lomax.”

The best seats JUST WENT ON SALE!!! 🦇🦇🦇🦇 📅 When: Halloween Night-October 31st, 2026 🕢 Time: Doors 7PM | Show 8PM 📍 Where: Sevenwinds Casino 🎟️ Tickets: bit.ly/4gQcNl8 🦇🦇🦇🦇 Don't miss all your favorite MTV Classics like Crazy Train, I Don't Know, Mama I'm Comin' Home, Flying High, Bark At The Moon, Over The Mountain, No More Tears, along with Sabbath classics like War Pigs, Into The Void, Paranoid and sooo many more great metal classics from the massive Ozzy Osbourne library! Come see why this band is taking the Ozzy world by storm and selling out all over the country!

events.title: Them Coulee Boys
events.description: “A rollicking blend of bluegrass, folk, and rock and roll” - Folk Alley Soren Staff and Beau Janke—co-founders of folk/rock/Americana outfit Them Coulee Boys—met as camp counselors in northern Wisconsin in 2011. Their weekend workshopping of Avett Brothers and classic country tunes led to original songs and adding Soren’s brother Jens on mandolin, Neil Krause on electric bass and Stas Hable on drums. The band’s name is a nod to the glacial melt-carved river valleys they call home, known by early French fur trappers as coulees. Known for wild swings of emotion during sets, it is not unusual to see fans in tears and minutes later dancing with abandon. The honesty and ability to talk and sing about the feelings and emotions that shape them has endeared them to a growing group of fans and friends. Over the course of five albums, the band has garnered international attention and earned press in Americana UK, American Songwriter, Ditty TV, Folk Alley, and The Bluegrass Situation.

events.title: Tennessee Whiskey Revival
events.description: Honoring the integrity of the original Chris Stapleton compositions while infusing each performance with soulful energy and expressive musicianship, the band offers a sound that is both authentic and fresh. Since their 2025 debut, Tennessee Whiskey Revival (featuring Scott Kirby) has quickly established itself as a premier Chris Stapleton tribute, captivating audiences across the Northwoods and beyond. To the stage they bring their roots - rock, bluegrass, soul, folk, country, and other influences - merging their colorful musicianship in tribute to musician and songwriter Chris Stapleton. In seizing this opportunity, their sound is designed like no other band paying tribute to the legendary performer Chris Stapleton. While their construct maintains the integrity of Chris Stapleton originals, their soulful energy and heartfelt solos color each masterfully composed song. The vibe of the musicians is fresh and forward. "Scott Kirby’s Tennessee Whiskey Revival—a heartfelt tribute to Chris Stapleton—delivers powerhouse vocals, exceptional musicianship, and pure soul. A must-see performance!" (Sandra Madden, Executive Director, Campanile Center for the Arts)
